name: Epoch Cassette Vision
description: A Japanese console released by Epoch in 1981, with simple graphics and controls built into the console. Unusually, the processor sat in each cartridge rather than in the console. It was a hit before the Famicom arrived, selling about 400,000 units.
curiosities: It launched at ¥13,500, with games at ¥4,000.
The controls are knobs and buttons on the console itself, not separate controllers.
Only eleven games were released commercially.
A cheaper Cassette Vision Jr. followed in 1983 at ¥5,000.
story: Epoch, a Japanese toy company, released the Cassette Vision in 1981.
Simple and cheap, it sold well in Japan before the Famicom arrived.
Epoch followed it with the Super Cassette Vision in 1984.
